what_worked: Strong thesis with purposeful narrative arc, good caveats slide, and clean visual hierarchy throughout.
fix_next: Median values for most categories are materially wrong versus the reference dataset; recompute all medians and MRR/builder figures from scratch.
verdict: Compelling story undermined by systematically incorrect median and per-builder figures.
factual_error_detail: Slide 6/21: AI median $446 (ref $503), Marketing $1,586 (ref $2,369.50), Dev Tools $185 (ref $635), Health & Fitness $392 (ref $662.50), Analytics $1,294 (ref $419), Education $2,142 (ref $2,435). Slide 14: AI MRR/builder $9,167 (ref ~$11,963), Marketing MRR/builder $10,583 (ref ~$31,364).

evidence.insight: Slide 10's B2B vs B2C AI split and slide 11's zero-revenue comparison go beyond chart description to reveal actionable buyer-type insight. Slide 12 grounds the thesis in specific company examples.
evidence.narrative: Clear three-act structure (crowded→wrong target→real yield) with a punchy thesis on slide 17 and actionable playbook on slide 18. Section dividers maintain rhythm.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 sets up three questions cleanly. Slide 3 establishes credibility. Slide 19 handles caveats well including small-n warnings and snapshot limitation. Audience (founders) is clear.
evidence.accuracy: At least 6 category medians on slides 6/21 are materially wrong vs reference (e.g., Analytics $1,294 vs ref $419, Marketing $1,586 vs ref $2,369.50). MRR/builder on slide 14 wrong for AI and Marketing. Systematic calculation error undermines core claims.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/gold palette, clean bar charts with direct labels, good use of whitespace. Scatter plot on slide 7 lacks axis values. Section dividers are slightly excessive (4 of 24 slides). Appendix tables are well-formatted.
evidence.ai_slop: none — deck avoids generic filler, every slide serves the argument
